# Tether

> Tether is a free, open source (MIT) project. It is a browser extension and local MCP server that lets AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and any MCP client) use the browser tabs a person shares, signed in as them. Tether runs entirely on the user's machine; what the agent reads goes to that agent's own model provider.

- Agents can read pages as an outline with element references, click, type, fill forms, navigate, upload files and take screenshots.
- Devtools: network requests with bodies, console messages and cookies.
- Sites can be restyled with UserCSS and changed with userscripts compatible with Stylus and Tampermonkey.
- Users stay in control: tabs are shared one at a time, agents ask before opening their own window, a visible cursor shows each action, and Pause holds the agent.
- Works with Chrome, Brave, Edge, Firefox and Zen.

## Links

- [Home](https://tether.udaysinh.me/): features, setup and FAQ
- [Guide](https://tether.udaysinh.me/guide/): how to let Claude Code or Codex use your real browser
- [Tether vs Gemini in Chrome](https://tether.udaysinh.me/vs/gemini-in-chrome/): how the two differ
- [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tether/bdkhlojbkkldeehiolelnmnpaanjdncc): the extension for Chrome, Brave and Edge
- [Firefox Add-ons](https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/tether/): the extension for Firefox and Zen
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tether-browser): the local MCP host, `npm install -g tether-browser`
- [Source code](https://github.com/udaysinh-git/tether): GitHub repository, MIT licence
- [Community](https://discord.gg/UcB8z8u4JP): the KuroLabs Discord, where the #tether channel has ideas, feedback and early builds
